description:
pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs:236-244: EvidenceIndex::build walks findings and tests 'if !keys.contains(&k)' — a linear scan of the keys Vec for each new finding, yielding O(N²) where N is total findings.

In realistic deployments N stays modest (a few dozen lints × a chain of a few certs = order 100s). The O(N²) cost is invisible.

At scale this matters: a batch evidence-pack run over hundreds of chains aggregated into one report — N could reach 10⁴ — runs into 10⁸ key compares. The keys are (Option<[u8;32]>, Option<usize>), so each compare is cheap, but cumulatively non-trivial.

Trivial fix: use std::collections::HashSet<EvidenceKey> to track seen keys plus a Vec for insertion order. Drop-in replacement, same observable output.

Not P0 because no production batch shape exists yet, but easy to land and removes a future foot-gun.
title: EvidenceIndex::build is O(N²) over findings via Vec::contains
